paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jesus doesn't just fill your nets. He calls you to follow Him. Simon had worked hard all night and caught nothing, and Jesus still said, "Put out into deep water and let down your nets for a catch." Simon answered, "But because You say so, I will let down the nets." (Luke 5:4-5)

Look at what happens next, because it matters. The catch is so big that both boats begin to sink, and when Simon sees it, he falls at Jesus' knees and says, "Go away from me, Lord, for I am a sinful man." (Luke 5:7-8) I think he saw how holy Jesus was and felt how small he was next to Him. And Jesus didn't go away, but said, "Do not be afraid," and then, "From now on you will catch men." (Luke 5:10)

So here's what it means for you, baker. Jesus doesn't wait for you to be ready or spotless before He gives you a job, and He meets you right in the middle of your worn-out nights and your not-good-enough moments. I know what that feels like, because God sent an angel to call me out of a dusty junk drawer. They "left everything and followed Him" (Luke 5:11), and the best catch of your life is still not as good as Him.
